papers.title: Comparative study of the influence of tool diameter on axial tool wear, cavity formation, and surface integrity in electro discharge drilling of Ti–6Al–4V
papers.abstract: Electro discharge drilling (EDD) is widely used for producing deep, high-aspect-ratio holes in difficult-to-machine materials such as Ti-6Al-4V. However, excessive tool wear, limited cavity depth, and poor surface integrity remain major challenges, particularly with small-diameter electrodes. This study investigates the influence of tool diameter on EDD performance using tubular copper electrodes of 0.3, 0.5, and 0.7 mm diameter. The effects of discharge current, pulse-on time, pulse-off time, and capacitance were evaluated using the single-factor-at-a-time method. Material removal rate (MRR), tool wear rate, axial tool wear, cavity depth, and surface roughness were used to assess machining performance. Increasing discharge energy improved MRR but also increased tool wear and surface roughness. The effect of tool diameter on MRR depended on the discharge parameter: the 0.3 mm electrode produced the highest MRR under current and pulse-off time variations, whereas the 0.5 mm electrode achieved higher MRR under several pulse-on time and capacitance conditions. In contrast, the 0.7 mm electrode produced the deepest cavities (8.5−9.0 mm), lower axial tool wear, and superior surface integrity under moderate discharge conditions. Optical profilometry and scanning electron microscopy revealed debris adhesion and micro-crack formation under high-energy machining conditions. The results demonstrate that optimum EDD performance requires an appropriate combination of discharge parameters and tool diameter rather than maximizing discharge energy alone.
papers.venue: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers Part E Journal of Process Mechanical Engineering

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究电火花钻孔对Ti-6Al-4V的加工性能，但未涉及增材制造或后处理对疲劳/力学性能的影响，与该方向不直接相关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper concerns electro discharge drilling of conventional Ti-6Al-4V, not additive manufacturing, and it does not evaluate post-processing effects on fatigue or mechanical performance.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究电火花钻孔中电极直径对加工效率和表面质量的影响。
summary_zh.method: 采用0.3、0.5、0.7mm铜电极，通过单因素实验评估放电参数对MRR、磨损和表面粗糙度的影响。
summary_zh.result: 0.7mm电极产生更深孔腔、更小磨损和更好表面，而0.3mm电极在部分参数下MRR最高。
summary_zh.validation: 使用光学轮廓仪和扫描电镜观察表面缺陷与显微裂纹。

summary_en.motivation: This study investigates the influence of tool diameter on machining efficiency and surface quality in electro discharge drilling of Ti-6Al-4V.
summary_en.method: Tubular copper electrodes of 0.3, 0.5, and 0.7 mm diameter were used with a single-factor method to evaluate the effects of discharge parameters on MRR, tool wear, and surface roughness.
summary_en.result: The 0.7 mm electrode produced deeper cavities (8.5–9.0 mm), lower axial tool wear, and superior surface integrity, while the 0.3 mm electrode achieved higher MRR under certain current and pulse-off time conditions.
summary_en.validation: Surface integrity and defect formation were characterized using optical profilometry and scanning electron microscopy.

papers.title: Selective laser melting of CoCrMo-Ti6Al4V bimetallic composites: fabrication, characterization, and cytocompatibility
papers.abstract: Bimetallic structures integrating Ti6Al4V and CoCrMo alloys present a promising solution for advanced orthopedic implants by combining high fracture toughness with excellent wear resistance. However, the direct fabrication of these dissimilar metals via Selective Laser Melting (SLM) is significantly hindered by metallurgical incompatibility and high residual stress, which typically lead to interfacial delamination and curling deformation. In this study, a Ti6Al4V-CoCrMo bimetallic composite was successfully developed using SLM. To overcome manufacturing defects, a loose CoCrMo transition layer was employed as a mechanical buffer to accommodate residual stresses, while optimized external support structures provided physical anchoring to suppress geometric distortion and edge curling.The microstructural evolution, elemental distribution, and phase composition were systematically characterized using electron microscopy and diffraction techniques. The mechanical performance was evaluated through hardness and sliding wear tests, while the biological response was assessed using bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). The results indicated that the three-layer architecture effectively eliminated macro-defects and ensured structural integrity. The composite exhibited a substantial enhancement in surface hardness and wear resistance, achieving performance levels comparable to monolithic CoCrMo alloy.Fracture analysis revealed a cohesive failure mode within the transition layer, demonstrating robust metallurgical bonding between the dissimilar components.Furthermore, in vitro assessments confirmed excellent cytocompatibility and healthy cell proliferation on the composite surfaces. This research establishes a reliable fabrication methodology for complex bimetallic components, offering broad application prospects in personalized medical devices, joint replacements, and tissue engineering.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究SLM制备CoCrMo-Ti6Al4V双金属复合材料的工艺与力学性能，虽涉及Ti6Al4V，但核心是异种金属结合而非纯Ti6Al4V的机械/疲劳性能。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not report tensile, fatigue, or S-N behavior of bulk Ti-6Al-4V; its focus is on bimetallic composite fabrication, hardness/wear, and cytocompatibility, with no fatigue or monotonic mechanical characterization relevant to the Ti-6Al-4V AM fatigue direction.

summary_zh.motivation: CoCrMo与Ti6Al4V异种金属直接SLM成形困难，需解决界面开裂和残余应力问题。
summary_zh.method: 采用松散CoCrMo过渡层和外部支撑结构实现SLM双金属复合材料的无缺陷成形。
summary_zh.result: 三层结构消除了宏观缺陷，硬度和耐磨性接近纯CoCrMo，界面结合良好且细胞相容性优异。
summary_zh.validation: 通过硬度、滑动磨损、断口分析及骨髓间充质干细胞培养进行验证。

summary_en.motivation: The study aims to overcome metallurgical incompatibility and residual stress issues that prevent direct selective laser melting of CoCrMo-Ti6Al4V bimetallic structures for orthopedic implants.
summary_en.method: A loose CoCrMo transition layer and optimized external supports were used as mechanical buffers to accommodate residual stresses and suppress geometric distortion during SLM fabrication.
summary_en.result: The three-layer architecture eliminated macro-defects, achieved hardness and wear resistance comparable to monolithic CoCrMo, and showed cohesive interfacial failure with excellent in vitro cytocompatibility.
summary_en.validation: Fabricated samples were validated through hardness testing, sliding wear tests, fracture analysis, and BMSC cell culture assessments.
